unknowns.question: Where does the page's content come from: the GitHub Releases API at build time, or the releases/notes/*.md files in the repo? The files need no token but include unpublished drafts and miss bodies swapped by hand before Publish (the v1-launch-notes trigger).

What makes the site rebuild when a release is published? deploy-docs.yml only runs on pushes touching docs/** or a manual dispatch, so the page goes stale unless a release-published trigger (or the file-based source) covers it.
How do other open-source repos and Starlight plugins build a releases page, and is there an off-the-shelf plugin that fits?
What sits above the release list: a header only, or some static prose? Let the survey of other repos show the done thing.
Do release-candidate pre-releases appear on the page, and how are they marked?

knowns.fact: The docs site is Astro Starlight in docs/, deployed to GitHub Pages by deploy-docs.yml, which runs on pushes to main touching docs/** or workflow_dispatch; dependencies are pinned and add-ons kept minimal.
Releases are drafts created by release.yml on a v* tag push from releases/notes/<tag>.md, rc tags marked pre-release, and Zac publishes each by hand.
No pagination: Ang expects few releases, so the page shows them all, newest first.
